llm.summary: This skill is a markdown-only prompt generator for educational note-card images, with no evidence of hidden execution, credential access, persistence, or exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: Read and AskUserQuestion are proportionate for reading the split documentation and asking for missing title information; Write/Edit are declared but not used by the artifact instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown documentation and examples only; no executable scripts, package installers, network calls, or background setup were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are mostly scoped to prompt construction, but the trigger list includes broad style and fandom terms that could activate the skill outside the intended educational-card task.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background workers, credential/session access, local indexing, privilege escalation, or destructive behavior appears in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe generating structured AI image prompts for Chinese educational knowledge cards, posters, exercises, and answer pages.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, be aware that generic triggers such as style names, fandom labels, or Minecraft-related terms may invoke this skill when you only meant to discuss those topics. The skill otherwise appears low risk and focused on prompt generation; consider narrowing triggers and removing unused Write/Edit authority if you maintain it.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger list is supported by artifact evidence and should be narrowed, but the skill’s actual behavior remains limited to generating educational image prompts, so this does not justify a Review verdict by itself.
